outcome: Demographic characteristics (age, gender, first-born status, maternal age, prenatal assistance)
Clinical characteristics (low birthweight, prematurity, breastfeeding duration, early artificial food introduction)
Laboratory characteristics (total cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol, triglycerides) in obese children and adolescents
cohort: The study included 89 obese children and adolescents admitted to an obesity ambulatory in the southeastern region of Brazil.
finding: The study found that while all obese patients had at least one altered biochemical test, factors such as cesarean delivery, low birthweight, prematurity, and early introduction of artificial food were not predominant among them.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was not predominant among the obese patients (42.6%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from medical records of children admitted to an obesity ambulatory, with a mean age of 68.9 months.
birth_weight: Variable; 6.7% of the cohort had low birthweight.
gest_age: Variable; 8.7% of the cohort had prematurity.
